Entry Mill Taxes of the Riverlands Waterwheels and windmills may seem quiet, but they often belong to those who can collect their share of the grinding mill. Farmers had to turn their harvests into flour, millers relied on it and local lords received a steady income; disputes over water rights, canals and priorities were never just petty disputes. Any break in the place of origin, checkpoints, shipping schedules, debts and protection fees will immediately make the nobles in the distance feel the changes in price and power.

They may not necessarily understand ledgers, but they know the true weight of a bag of salt and a nail on the road.

Some people turn raw materials into tools, cloth and medicine, others set festivals and taboos for exchange; wealth is piled up by many hands, and rarely belongs to just one name.
